rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for asking why, including before a verb or noun phrase.

example.english: Why are you back so early?
example.jyutping: dim2 gaai2 nei5 gam3 zou2 faan1 lei4 aa3

rows.note: Use this casual, often more emphatic alternative when asking why someone is doing something or why a situation is so.

example.english: Why are you still not leaving?
example.jyutping: zou6 me1 nei5 zung6 m4 zau2 aa3

rows.note: Use this for the causal-linking sense of “that is why” or “therefore,” rather than for a direct question.

example.english: He was sick, so that's why he didn't go to work.
example.jyutping: keoi5 beng6 zo2 so2 ji5 mou5 faan1 gung1

rows.note: Use this pattern specifically to make a rhetorical suggestion such as “Why don’t you V?”

example.jyutping: dim2 gaai2 m4 sik6 maai4 sin1 aa3
